new_value:
{"notes":"HSA/FSA flag (is_hsa_fsa) — decision + open question (2026-07-01, tuily):

KEEP the payments.is_hsa_fsa column. FT9 (docs: product/features/FT-signup-payment-flow.md) makes 'HSA/FSA card flagged correctly on receipt' a GO-LIVE acceptance criterion, so the per-payment flag is required.

BUT the detection mechanism FT9 assumes is NOT possible. Confirmed against current Stripe docs:
- Stripe has NO API-level HSA/FSA detection. Support page: 'Stripe does not provide API-level detection for HSA/FSA cards.'
- PaymentMethod.card exposes no health-benefit field and NO full BIN/IIN — only last4. funding is credit|debit|prepaid|unknown (prepaid is a weak, unreliable proxy).
- So FT9's 'HSA/FSA card detected on the Stripe Customer object' cannot be implemented — Stripe surfaces no such data. This resolves the open standup item (2026-06-08: validate Stripe HSA/FSA config steps).
- Stripe's own receipt shows nothing about HSA/FSA and only itemizes invoice/subscription payments (ours is a one-off PaymentIntent) — hence the custom Resend receipt (FT11/D11) is required.
- Acceptance itself is purely account config: HSA/FSA-eligible MCC (8011/8099). SIGIS/IIAS only applies to merchants selling products, not a medical service — so we're on the simpler MCC path.

PROPOSED populator: user self-select checkbox ('I'm paying with an HSA/FSA card') → is_hsa_fsa. SAQ-A-safe (no PAN), self-reported (not financial truth). funding==prepaid could prefill only.

OPEN — needs PM sign-off: is a self-select checkbox acceptable to satisfy the FT9 receipt-flag requirement, given Stripe can't auto-detect? Checkbox NOT built yet (deferred out of the test-mode demo)."}

KEEP the payments.is_hsa_fsa column. FT9 (docs: product/features/FT-signup-payment-flow.md) makes 'HSA/FSA card flagged correctly on receipt' a GO-LIVE acceptance criterion, so the per-payment flag is required.

BUT the detection mechanism FT9 assumes is NOT possible. Confirmed against current Stripe docs:
- Stripe has NO API-level HSA/FSA detection. Support page: 'Stripe does not provide API-level detection for HSA/FSA cards.'
- PaymentMethod.card exposes no health-benefit field and NO full BIN/IIN — only last4. funding is credit|debit|prepaid|unknown (prepaid is a weak, unreliable proxy).
- So FT9's 'HSA/FSA card detected on the Stripe Customer object' cannot be implemented — Stripe surfaces no such data. This resolves the open standup item (2026-06-08: validate Stripe HSA/FSA config steps).
- Stripe's own receipt shows nothing about HSA/FSA and only itemizes invoice/subscription payments (ours is a one-off PaymentIntent) — hence the custom Resend receipt (FT11/D11) is required.
- Acceptance itself is purely account config: HSA/FSA-eligible MCC (8011/8099). SIGIS/IIAS only applies to merchants selling products, not a medical service — so we're on the simpler MCC path.

PROPOSED populator: user self-select checkbox ('I'm paying with an HSA/FSA card') → is_hsa_fsa. SAQ-A-safe (no PAN), self-reported (not financial truth). funding==prepaid could prefill only.

OPEN — needs PM sign-off: is a self-select checkbox acceptable to satisfy the FT9 receipt-flag requirement, given Stripe can't auto-detect? Checkbox NOT built yet (deferred out of the test-mode demo)."}

{"id":"pbh-bws.22","title":"Build: Stripe Payment Element + HSA/FSA","description":"Payment step inside SAQ-A boundary; HSA/FSA support.","notes":"HSA/FSA flag (is_hsa_fsa) — decision + open question (2026-07-01, tuily):

KEEP the payments.is_hsa_fsa column. FT9 (docs: product/features/FT-signup-payment-flow.md) makes 'HSA/FSA card flagged correctly on receipt' a GO-LIVE acceptance criterion, so the per-payment flag is required.

BUT the detection mechanism FT9 assumes is NOT possible. Confirmed against current Stripe docs:
- Stripe has NO API-level HSA/FSA detection. Support page: 'Stripe does not provide API-level detection for HSA/FSA cards.'
- PaymentMethod.card exposes no health-benefit field and NO full BIN/IIN — only last4. funding is credit|debit|prepaid|unknown (prepaid is a weak, unreliable proxy).
- So FT9's 'HSA/FSA card detected on the Stripe Customer object' cannot be implemented — Stripe surfaces no such data. This resolves the open standup item (2026-06-08: validate Stripe HSA/FSA config steps).
- Stripe's own receipt shows nothing about HSA/FSA and only itemizes invoice/subscription payments (ours is a one-off PaymentIntent) — hence the custom Resend receipt (FT11/D11) is required.
- Acceptance itself is purely account config: HSA/FSA-eligible MCC (8011/8099). SIGIS/IIAS only applies to merchants selling products, not a medical service — so we're on the simpler MCC path.

PROPOSED populator: user self-select checkbox ('I'm paying with an HSA/FSA card') → is_hsa_fsa. SAQ-A-safe (no PAN), self-reported (not financial truth). funding==prepaid could prefill only.

OPEN — needs PM sign-off: is a self-select checkbox acceptable to satisfy the FT9 receipt-flag requirement, given Stripe can't auto-detect? - 360-2502  Landing booking section 'Start With a Brain Health assessment & Consultation' (First/Last/Email + Includes checklist + $149 / HSA-FSA note). Ref: apps/funnel .../signup/SignupForm.tsx + marketing IntakeForm block.
- 360-2854  Modal 1 'Welcome, {name}' details (DOB, gender, ZIP, phone, education, concerns). Ref: apps/funnel .../details/DetailsForm.tsx.

- Flow lives ENTIRELY on the marketing site, presented as a MODAL sequence.
- Funnel /get-started stepper was DEMO scaffolding — not the production surface (retire it).
- Scope = full end-to-end.

BACKEND RECOMMENDATION — consolidate server logic into marketing via shared workspace packages (not copy-paste, not cross-app API):

DESIGN -> STEP MAPPING (all 5 already exist as funnel DEMO code, being re-homed to marketing):
- 360-2502  Landing booking section 'Start With a Brain Health assessment & Consultation' (First/Last/Email + Includes checklist + $149 / HSA-FSA note). Ref: apps/funnel .../signup/SignupForm.tsx + marketing IntakeForm block.
- 360-2854  Modal 1 'Welcome, {name}' details (DOB, gender, ZIP, phone, education, concerns). Ref: apps/funnel .../details/DetailsForm.tsx.
- 466-245 / 360-3214  Modal 2 'Almost there!' terms; scroll-to-enable -> 'Continue With Payment'. Ref: apps/funnel .../consent/ConsentForm.tsx.
- 360-3226  Modal 3 'Payment' — Stripe Embedded Checkout. Ref: apps/funnel .../payment/PaymentStep.tsx.

DECISIONS (from user):
- Flow lives ENTIRELY on the marketing site, presented as a MODAL sequence.
- Funnel /get-started stepper was DEMO scaffolding — not the production surface (retire it).
- Scope = full end-to-end.

BACKEND RECOMMENDATION — consolidate server logic into marketing via shared workspace packages (not copy-paste, not cross-app API):
- @pbh/db       Drizzle schema + migrations + Neon client (from apps/funnel/src/db)
- @pbh/payments Stripe server helpers + Checkout Session + webhook (from apps/funnel/src/lib/stripe)
- @pbh/linus    enrollment client (from apps/funnel/src/lib/linus)
- Re-home the 4 step server actions (createAccount, completeProfile, recordConsent, createAssessmentCheckoutSession/finalizeCheckoutSession) as MARKETING server actions calling those packages.
Rejected: marketing-calls-funnel-API (cross-origin CORS/cookie/iframe-Stripe friction); copy-paste rebuild (duplication/drift).

SHARED UI -> promote to @pbh/ui (shared UI only, never business logic): StepHeader, FieldError, Label, field/textarea class constants, 'Myself / Someone Else' segmented control, styled <select>.

OPEN ITEMS (non-blocking):
- Does the funnel keep /assessments + /login? If yes -> they consume @pbh/db/@pbh/linus; if funnel fully retired -> fold packages into marketing.
- Design tokens: Figma uses teal (#006e8a primary/CTA, #f5f3ee input bg, #224b60 Includes card) vs codebase Cognitive Sanctuary (navy #041632, forest #446558). Confirm whether teal is new brand primary or maps to existing tokens (see pbh-bws.39).

[ ] Build modal StepFlow state machine + 5 screens on marketing (open, transitions, terms-scroll gating, validation)

[ ] Reconcile design tokens
[ ] QA: test-mode payment through the modal (account -> consent row -> Stripe test card -> enrollment) + webhook backstop

{"id":"pbh-ggr","title":"Booking StepFlow (5 Figma designs) — marketing-site modal, end-to-end","description":"Implement the 5 Figma booking/assessment StepFlow designs as a MODAL sequence on the marketing site, full end-to-end (real account, consent, Stripe payment, DB writes, Linus enrollment).

Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health

DESIGN -> STEP MAPPING (all 5 already exist as funnel DEMO code, being re-homed to marketing):
- 360-2502  Landing booking section 'Start With a Brain Health assessment & Consultation' (First/Last/Email + Includes checklist + $149 / HSA-FSA note). Ref: apps/funnel .../signup/SignupForm.tsx + marketing IntakeForm block.
- 360-2854  Modal 1 'Welcome, {name}' details (DOB, gender, ZIP, phone, education, concerns). Ref: apps/funnel .../details/DetailsForm.tsx.
- 466-245 / 360-3214  Modal 2 'Almost there!' terms; scroll-to-enable -> 'Continue With Payment'. Ref: apps/funnel .../consent/ConsentForm.tsx.
- 360-3226  Modal 3 'Payment' — Stripe Embedded Checkout. Ref: apps/funnel .../payment/PaymentStep.tsx.

DECISIONS (from user):
- Flow lives ENTIRELY on the marketing site, presented as a MODAL sequence.
- Funnel /get-started stepper was DEMO scaffolding — not the production surface (retire it).
- Scope = full end-to-end.

BACKEND RECOMMENDATION — consolidate server logic into marketing via shared workspace packages (not copy-paste, not cross-app API):
- @pbh/db       Drizzle schema + migrations + Neon client (from apps/funnel/src/db)
- @pbh/payments Stripe server helpers + Checkout Session + webhook (from apps/funnel/src/lib/stripe)
- @pbh/linus    enrollment client (from apps/funnel/src/lib/linus)
- Re-home the 4 step server actions (createAccount, completeProfile, recordConsent, createAssessmentCheckoutSession/finalizeCheckoutSession) as MARKETING server actions calling those packages.
Rejected: marketing-calls-funnel-API (cross-origin CORS/cookie/iframe-Stripe friction); copy-paste rebuild (duplication/drift).

SHARED UI -> promote to @pbh/ui (shared UI only, never business logic): StepHeader, FieldError, Label, field/textarea class constants, 'Myself / Someone Else' segmented control, styled <select>.

OPEN ITEMS (non-blocking):
- Does the funnel keep /assessments + /login? If yes -> they consume @pbh/db/@pbh/linus; if funnel fully retired -> fold packages into marketing.
- Design tokens: Figma uses teal (#006e8a primary/CTA, #f5f3ee input bg, #224b60 Includes card) vs codebase Cognitive Sanctuary (navy #041632, forest #446558). Confirm whether teal is new brand primary or maps to existing tokens (see pbh-bws.39).

SUB-WORK CHECKLIST:
[ ] Extract @pbh/db, @pbh/payments, @pbh/linus from apps/funnel
[ ] Promote shared UI primitives to @pbh/ui
[ ] Build modal StepFlow state machine + 5 screens on marketing (open, transitions, terms-scroll gating, validation)
[ ] Tina landing block for 360-2502 (booking entry + Includes + $149)
[ ] Re-home 4 server actions to marketing; wire Stripe Embedded Checkout + webhook + Linus enrollment end-to-end
[ ] Reconcile design tokens
[ ] QA: test-mode payment through the modal (account -> consent row -> Stripe test card -> enrollment) + webhook backstop

RELATES TO: pbh-bws.17 (signup/consent/payment surfaces — was 'no Figma', now superseded by these designs on marketing), pbh-bws.20 (landing page), pbh-bws.21 (account creation + consent), pbh-bws.15 (component-library extension from V1), pbh-bws.24 (signed-token handoff), pbh-bws.39 (Stripe Appearance/brand tokens).","notes":"OPEN ITEMS RESOLVED (2026-07-08):

{"id":"pbh-bws.43","title":"Linus API integration tests (unit + mocked HTTP/DB)","description":"The Linus API integration is the funnel's highest-stakes external seam (register subject + enroll in cognitive assessments post-payment) and is currently UNTESTED. Add tests covering apps/funnel/src/lib/linus/* and apps/funnel/src/app/assessments/register-and-enroll.ts.

Depends on pbh-bws.42 (vitest harness must exist first).

Two layers:

1. Pure-unit (no network/DB):
   - extractReportData (client.ts): base64 reportData out of the array report shape.
   - buildRegisterInput + MissingDateOfBirthError (build-register-input.ts).
   - toSexAssignedAtBirth mapping + OTHER default.
   - getCampaigns env switch (campaigns.ts) via VERCEL_ENV (sandbox vs prod ids).
   - getLinusConfig missing-var error message (env.ts).

2. Mocked HTTP/DB (higher value):
   - client.ts: mock fetch to cover getAccessToken token caching/refresh (60s safety margin), bearer + User-Agent headers, and LinusApiError {status, body} thrown on non-2xx.
   - register-and-enroll.ts concurrency/idempotency logic (mock the DB layer):
     - ensureRegistered claim-win / deferred / error outcomes and retryOnContention behavior (webhook throws->500->Stripe redelivers vs client shows success).
     - storeParticipantId unique-violation (23505 / PgErrorCode.UniqueViolation) fallback to already-stored id.
     - resolveEnrollments 4-step ladder, esp. the invariant: NEVER re-POST an active/started enrollment (Linus enrollSubject mints a new one for 'started', orphaning the report).

Note: no HTTP-mocking pattern exists in the repo yet - establish one (vitest vi.mock / vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...)); it becomes the template for future funnel integration tests.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"brizolla.tuily@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-08T17:16:39Z","created_by":"tuily","updated_at":"2026-07-08T17:16:39Z"}

{"id":"pbh-chu","title":"Implement "Choose How to Start" first-login welcome screen (funnel)","description":"Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=1088-1628&m=dev

Post-login "Choose How to Start" screen in the funnel app. Headline + subcopy and two cards: "Talk to an Expert" (CTA: Start With Navigator) and "Start with Assessments" (CTA: Start Assessments). Shown ONLY on a user's first login.

## Decisions
- Start Assessments -> redirect to /assessments (no /dashboard route exists; it is the de-facto dashboard today).
- First-login state -> new nullable users.welcomeSeenAt timestamptz (Clerk is NOT integrated, so DB is the only store).
- Scope: core screen only (headline + subcopy + two cards/CTAs) inside the funnel's existing minimal layout. NO top nav / Profile dropdown / footer chrome (deferred).
- Start With Navigator -> placeholder alert() referencing the companion task; wired up separately.

## Implementation
1. DB: add welcomeSeenAt: timestamp("welcome_seen_at", { withTimezone: true }) (nullable) to packages/db/src/schema/users.ts (match linusRegistrationClaimedAt style). Run pnpm --filter @pbh/db run db:generate -> commit new packages/db/src/migrations/0008_*.sql. Migrations apply on PROD deploy only (apps/funnel/vercel.json); for local/preview apply the column to the dev DB via the db-migrate skill.
2. Gate in one place: in apps/funnel/src/app/assessments/actions.ts (registerAndEnroll, ~line 57) change post-login redirect from /assessments to /welcome.
3. New route apps/funnel/src/app/welcome/ (mirror assessments/ conventions):
   - page.tsx: async server component + guard. Read ASSESSMENT_UID_COOKIE; missing -> redirect("/login"). Load user; if welcomeSeenAt set -> redirect("/assessments"). Else render centered <main flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center> + Container size="narrow" + Heading + subcopy + two Cards, reusing @pbh/ui (Button, Container, Heading, Card).
   - WelcomeActions.tsx: "use client" sibling with the two CTAs. Start With Navigator -> Button onClick alert placeholder. Start Assessments -> <form action={markWelcomeSeen}> submit Button.
   - actions.ts: "use server" markWelcomeSeen(): resolve uid from ASSESSMENT_UID_COOKIE, db.update(users).set({ welcomeSeenAt: sql`now()` }).where(eq(users.id, uid)).returning({ id: users.id }) (mirror packages/booking/src/server/details-core.ts:102-115), then redirect("/assessments").

## Figma copy (verbatim)
- Headline: Choose How to Start
- Subcopy: You've already made an important decision for your brain health; now you can choose how you'd like to begin your care journey. Both options lead to a navigator and a clear plan - this just helps you pick the path that fits you best.
- Card 1: title "Talk to an Expert" / body "For individuals and care partners who feel overwhelmed, have many questions, or want guidance before diving into testing." / CTA "Start With Navigator"
- Card 2: title "Start with Assessments" / body "Best for individuals and care partners who are ready to move forward now and want results to guide the conversation." / CTA "Start Assessments"

## Conventions
Braces on every if; one component per file; token classes only (no raw hex).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fresh user (welcomeSeenAt null) lands on /welcome after login; sees the two-card screen.
- Start With Navigator shows placeholder alert; does not navigate.
- Start Assessments sets welcomeSeenAt and redirects to /assessments.
- Same user logging in again goes straight to /assessments (welcome not re-shown).
- Unauthenticated hit to /welcome redirects to /login.

## Verification
Apply column to dev DB, pnpm --filter funnel dev (:3001), log in with a fresh email -> /welcome; exercise both CTAs; re-login -> straight to /assessments; no-cookie /welcome -> /login. pnpm typecheck + lint changed files.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"brizolla.tuily@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-20T17:55:57Z","created_by":"tuily","updated_at":"2026-07-20T17:55:57Z"}

Post-login "Choose How to Start" screen in the funnel app. Headline + subcopy and two cards: "Talk to an Expert" (CTA: Start With Navigator) and "Start with Assessments" (CTA: Start Assessments). Shown ONLY on a user's first login.

## Decisions
- Start Assessments -> redirect to /assessments (no /dashboard route exists; it is the de-facto dashboard today).
- First-login state -> new nullable users.welcomeSeenAt timestamptz (Clerk is NOT integrated, so DB is the only store).
- Scope: core screen only (headline + subcopy + two cards/CTAs) inside the funnel's existing minimal layout. NO top nav / Profile dropdown / footer chrome (deferred).
- Start With Navigator -> placeholder alert() referencing the companion task; wired up separately.

## Implementation
1. DB: add welcomeSeenAt: timestamp("welcome_seen_at", { withTimezone: true }) (nullable) to packages/db/src/schema/users.ts (match linusRegistrationClaimedAt style). Run pnpm --filter @pbh/db run db:generate -> commit new packages/db/src/migrations/0008_*.sql. Migrations apply on PROD deploy only (apps/funnel/vercel.json); for local/preview apply the column to the dev DB via the db-migrate skill.
2. Gate in one place: in apps/funnel/src/app/assessments/actions.ts (registerAndEnroll, ~line 57) change post-login redirect from /assessments to /welcome.
3. New route apps/funnel/src/app/welcome/ (mirror assessments/ conventions):
   - page.tsx: async server component + guard. Read ASSESSMENT_UID_COOKIE; missing -> redirect("/login"). Load user; if welcomeSeenAt set -> redirect("/assessments"). Else render centered <main flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center> + Container size="narrow" + Heading + subcopy + two Cards, reusing @pbh/ui (Button, Container, Heading, Card).
   - WelcomeActions.tsx: "use client" sibling with the two CTAs. Start With Navigator -> Button onClick alert placeholder. Start Assessments -> <form action={markWelcomeSeen}> submit Button.
   - actions.ts: "use server" markWelcomeSeen(): resolve uid from ASSESSMENT_UID_COOKIE, db.update(users).set({ welcomeSeenAt: sql`now()` }).where(eq(users.id, uid)).returning({ id: users.id }) (mirror packages/booking/src/server/details-core.ts:102-115), then redirect("/assessments").

## Figma copy (verbatim)
- Headline: Choose How to Start
- Subcopy: You've already made an important decision for your brain health; now you can choose how you'd like to begin your care journey. Both options lead to a navigator and a clear plan - this just helps you pick the path that fits you best.
- Card 1: title "Talk to an Expert" / body "For individuals and care partners who feel overwhelmed, have many questions, or want guidance before diving into testing." / CTA "Start With Navigator"
- Card 2: title "Start with Assessments" / body "Best for individuals and care partners who are ready to move forward now and want results to guide the conversation." / CTA "Start Assessments"

Braces on every if; one component per file; token classes only (no raw hex).

- Fresh user (welcomeSeenAt null) lands on /welcome after login; sees the two-card screen.
- Start With Navigator shows placeholder alert; does not navigate.
- Start Assessments sets welcomeSeenAt and redirects to /assessments.
- Same user logging in again goes straight to /assessments (welcome not re-shown).
- Unauthenticated hit to /welcome redirects to /login.

## Verification

{"description":"After the user submits their email in the marketing booking flow, resume them at the correct point. NEW users go straight into the modal at the first step; RETURNING (known) users see a "Welcome back" screen and must confirm via an emailed link before resuming at their first incomplete step. If everything is already complete, hand off to the funnel.

Figma:
- Welcome-back screen ("Already in database"): https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=896-1479&m=dev

## Flow
1. Booking form email submit -> resolveBookingProgress(email) looks up the user.
2. NEW email -> create user (createAccountCore) -> open modal at "details" (no confirmation needed; nothing to protect).
3. RETURNING email (user exists, not fully complete) -> show the "Welcome back, {firstName}" modal (Figma 896-1479) and SEND a confirmation email. Do NOT open the step modal yet.
4. User clicks the emailed magic link -> verify token -> resume the booking modal at the FIRST INCOMPLETE step (details -> consent -> payment) computed by resolveBookingProgress.
5. Already fully complete (details + consent + succeeded payment) -> hand off to funnel /login?email= (same as DoneStep) -> /assessments.

## Welcome back screen (Figma 896-1479, "Extra Information" card)
- Title: "Welcome back, {firstName}"
- Body: "You already started the process previously. We’ve sent you an email. Please check your inbox, and confirm this is you."
- CTA: "Continue Where I left" (re-send/return affordance; the actual resume happens via the emailed link).
- Rendered as a modal/card over the booking section; reuse the existing Modal shell (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/Modal.tsx) + @pbh/ui + tokens.

## Current behavior (to change)
- BookingStepFlow.tsx uses a useState stepIndex over MODAL_STEPS = ["details","consent","payment","done"]; start() HARDCODES setStepIndex(0). advance() uses Math.min, so starting mid-sequence already works.
- Email is collected by inline SignupForm (first/last/email) -> signupAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts) -> createAccountCore (packages/booking/src/server/signup-core.ts), which INSERTs a users row and REJECTS duplicate emails ("account already exists"). Must change to lookup-or-create.

## Completeness signals (all NEW reads; consents/payments are write-only today)
- details incomplete if users.dateOfBirth is null (also stateOfResidence, phone, gender, educationLevel, patientIdentification; message optional). packages/db/src/schema/users.ts; set by details-core.ts.
- consent incomplete if no consents row for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/consents.ts.
- payment incomplete if no payments row with status="succeeded" for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/payments.ts (fulfill.ts recordSucceededPayment). A bare row is NOT sufficient (failed/refunded can exist).

## Implementation
1. resolveBookingProgress core in packages/booking/src/server/ (e.g. booking-progress.ts): normalize email; SELECT users WHERE email = ? (pattern in register-and-enroll.ts:499-519). No user -> createAccountCore -> step "details" (new-user path). User exists -> first incomplete step, or "complete". Returns { userId, email, firstName, step:"details"|"consent"|"payment"|"complete", isReturning:boolean }.
2. Returning + not complete -> render Welcome back modal + trigger sendResumeConfirmationEmail(userId). Wire signupAction accordingly.
3. Extend SignupState/SignupResult (packages/booking/src/types.ts) to carry step + isReturning (+ complete).
4. BookingStepFlow.start(): for the new-user path, setStepIndex(Math.max(0, MODAL_STEPS.indexOf(step))); for returning, show Welcome back modal instead; if step==="complete", navigate to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_FUNNEL_URL}/login?email=... (reuse DoneStep handoff).
5. Magic-link resume: verify route validates the token and opens the booking modal at the resolved first-incomplete step.

## Email confirmation infrastructure (NEW PREREQUISITE - none exists today)
There is NO email-sending setup in the repo (no resend/nodemailer/sendgrid/ses, no token/verify code). This feature needs:
- An email-sending capability + provider (recommend Resend; works cleanly on Vercel) + a confirmation email template.
- A confirmation token: signed (HMAC/JWT, short TTL) OR a DB table (e.g. booking_resume_tokens with expiry) tied to userId + intended step; single-use.
- A verify/resume route that validates the token and enters the resumed flow.
This is sizable and separable; consider splitting it into its own prerequisite sub-task that this one depends on.

## Security / privacy
The email confirmation is the mitigation for unauthenticated resume + PII/enumeration: DO NOT open the step modal or reveal stored data on bare email entry. To avoid account enumeration, show the same "we’ve sent you an email" outcome whether or not the email exists (only send the email when it does). Tokens must be single-use + short-lived. Revisit with real auth (resolveBookingUserId is a TODO(clerk)).

## Acceptance criteria
- New email -> modal opens at details (no email confirmation).
- Returning email (partial) -> Welcome back modal shown + confirmation email sent; step modal NOT opened until the emailed link is clicked; link resumes at the correct first incomplete step (consent if details done; payment if details+consent done).
- Fully-onboarded/paid email -> handed off to funnel /login -> /assessments.
- Bare email entry never reveals whether an account exists nor exposes stored PII; tokens single-use + expiring.
- Payment completeness uses status="succeeded", not just a row.

## Verification
Seed users at each state (new/partial/complete) in a test DB. pnpm --filter marketing dev (:3000); submit each email and confirm: new -> details; returning -> Welcome back + email; click link -> resumes at expected step; complete -> funnel handoff. pnpm typecheck + lint."}

If user exists, compute first incomplete step in order (details -> consent -> payment), else "complete". Return { status:"success", userId, email, firstName, step:"details"|"consent"|"payment"|"complete" } (or an error state mirroring SignupState). 2. Wire signupAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts) to call resolveBookingProgress instead of create-only createAccountCore.

5. SignupForm still collects first/last/email; for an existing user, ignore the entered name (keep stored record) and resume.

## Security / privacy note
Resuming by UNAUTHENTICATED email lets anyone enter an email to continue that account onboarding and reveals whether an email is registered (enumeration). This matches the current pre-auth scaffold (resolveBookingUserId is a TODO(clerk)) but must be revisited when real auth lands; the resolver should not leak stored PII to the client beyond what is needed to render the step.

- New email -> modal opens at details (unchanged for brand-new users).
- User with details but no consent -> opens at consent; details+consent but unpaid -> opens at payment.
- Fully-onboarded/paid user -> no modal; redirected to funnel /login?email= -> /assessments.
- Submitting a previously-registered email no longer shows "account already exists".
- Payment completeness uses status="succeeded", not just a row existing.

## Verification

{"id":"pbh-dgb","title":"Update the payment form to match the Figma design","description":"Restyle the booking payment step to match Figma.

Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=751-2529&m=dev
Pull the full frame via Figma MCP (get_design_context on 751-2529) for exact spacing/inputs.

## Design (node 751-2529, "Extra Information" modal card, has an X close)
- Header: "Payment" + subcopy "This service may be eligible for HSA/FSA reimbursement, depending on your plan. We can provide documentation to support submission."
- Checkout card: line item "Brain health assessment" + price "$149.00"; Email (prefilled); Payment method (card number, MM / YY, CVC + help, Cardholder name, Country or region = United States + ZIP); "Save my information for faster checkout" / "Pay securely on future visits" toggle; phone field with country flag.
- CTA: "Pay $149.00".

## KEY DECISION / RISK (resolve before implementing)
The current payment step uses Stripe EMBEDDED CHECKOUT — checkout.sessions with ui_mode="embedded_page" (packages/booking/src/server/checkout-core.ts, rendered by packages/booking/src/PaymentStep.tsx via payment/actions.ts createAssessmentCheckoutSession). That renders Stripe hosted UI in an iframe with limited layout control. The Figma shows a fully app-styled form. Achieving it likely means EITHER:
  (a) customize the Stripe Checkout appearance API (fonts/colors/radii to match @pbh/tokens) within Embedded Checkout layout constraints, OR
  (b) migrate to the Stripe Payment Element (PaymentIntent) for full layout/style control.
Decide and note the tradeoffs. Whichever path: the amount/currency/product name MUST still come from the Stripe catalog price (source of truth — reuse getAssessmentCatalogEntry; do NOT hardcode $149), and fulfillment (verifyAndRecordCheckout + the webhook backstop, finalizeCheckoutSession) must keep working.

## What to change
- packages/booking/src/PaymentStep.tsx (+ possibly checkout-core.ts / payment/actions.ts depending on path chosen).
- App-rendered chrome (header, "$X" summary, "Pay $X" CTA) uses @pbh/ui + tokens; the $ amount is dynamic from the catalog.

## Conventions
Token classes only, braces on every if, one component per file.

## Related
- pbh-eaw (Figma token audit) — align appearance with tokens.
- pbh-bq8 (resume-at-step) — payment is a step; keep resume compatible.
- Note prior sandbox findings: needs Stripe test keys + an ACTIVE price; restricted-key scopes must allow PaymentIntents/Checkout writes.

## Acceptance criteria
- Payment step matches the Figma frame (header + subcopy, checkout card w/ summary/email/card fields/save-info/phone, "Pay $X" CTA).
- Price/label come from the Stripe catalog (not hardcoded); payment completes with a test card and fulfillment still records + enrolls.
- Chosen Stripe approach (appearance API vs Payment Element) documented in the PR.
- Matches Figma in-browser (computed styles); no raw hex in app-rendered chrome.
- pnpm typecheck + lint changed files.

## Verification

{"id":"pbh-eaw","title":"Audit + reconcile UI code against Figma styles (Figma-covered screens)","description":"Verify the implemented UI follows the Figma design system (colors, typography, spacing, radii) for the screens that have Figma frames, produce a findings report, AND fix the drift. Enforcement today is convention-only (no stylelint/eslint color rules, no Figma Code Connect).

## Decisions (confirmed)
- Deliverable: a one-time audit REPORT of Figma-vs-code fidelity.
- Scope: only screens with Figma frames today — marketing landing + booking flow, "Choose How to Start" (node 1088-1628), "Welcome back" (node 896-1479).
- Fixes: INCLUDE reconciliation (same task expands tokens, migrates raw-hex, fixes fonts).

## Baseline facts
- Token source of truth: packages/tokens/theme.css (@pbh/tokens). Colors + two font families only (--font-headline "Larken", --font-body var(--font-inter,"Inter")). NO spacing/radius/type-scale tokens.
- Figma DOES define spacing/radius/color variables (via get_variable_defs on 1088-1628): button/primary/bg-color #006e8a, button/radius 40, button/padding 24x16, nav/gap 40, nav/padding 40/20, faq-section/*, footer/bg-color #eff6f9, footer/copyright-color #6f706e, text/secondary #6f706e, button/primary/text-color #ffffff.

## Part 1 — Audit (produce report)
For each in-scope screen, pull Figma (Figma MCP get_variable_defs / get_design_context / get_screenshot; nodes 1088-1628, 896-1479, plus marketing landing + booking frames) and diff against the rendered app: colors, typography (family/size/weight), spacing/padding/gap, radii. MEASURE the rendered CSS / in-browser output — do NOT trust class names alone (a class in source may not exist in the generated CSS). Commit a prioritized findings list as docs/design-audit.md (screen -> property -> Figma value vs code value -> severity).

## Part 2 — Reconcile (apply fixes)
- Tokens (packages/tokens/theme.css): add missing tokens Figma defines — a radius token (button/radius 40 -> e.g. --radius-pill), spacing tokens for recurring nav/button/footer/faq gaps + paddings, missing colors (#EFF6F9 as a surface token; reconcile #6f706e vs on-surface-variant #44474d). Re-expose new tokens in @theme inline; also expose :root tokens missing from @theme inline (e.g. --color-primary-fixed) if used.
- Raw-hex migration (~5 live usages -> token classes): apps/marketing/src/app/layout.tsx:72 (bg-[#EFF6F9]); apps/marketing/src/components/blocks/StackSections/StackSections.tsx:230 (#EFF6F9 + arbitrary shadow); apps/marketing/src/components/blocks/BenefitsList/BenefitsList.tsx:36 (#E2EFEF); apps/marketing/src/components/layout/Footer.tsx:7 (#EFF6F9); apps/funnel/src/app/assessments/AssessmentCard.tsx:30 (border-[#d8d8d8]).
- Fonts: standardize headline on Larken (align theme.css "Larken" with the Typekit "larken" loaded in apps/marketing/src/app/layout.tsx + apps/funnel/src/app/layout.tsx); define --font-inter consistently in funnel (or load Inter via next/font there); remove dead Gilda_Display wiring in marketing; update CLAUDE.md to drop the stale "Manrope" reference (real headline font is Larken).
- Conventions: token classes only, braces on every if, one component per file.

## Out of scope (possible follow-up)
Standing enforcement: stylelint/eslint no-hex rule, Figma Code Connect, visual-regression snapshots (could fold into pbh-d5a).

## Acceptance criteria
- docs/design-audit.md lists every Figma-vs-code discrepancy for in-scope screens (Figma value vs code value + severity).
- New spacing/radius/color tokens added + exposed to Tailwind; the ~5 raw-hex usages migrated (grep #[0-9a-fA-F]{6} in apps/** + packages/**/src shows no live off-token color).
- Font wiring consistent across both apps (headline = Larken; funnel body Inter resolves); CLAUDE.md updated.
- In-browser render of each in-scope screen visually matches the Figma frame.

## Verification
pnpm --filter marketing dev (:3000) + pnpm --filter funnel dev (:3001); load each in-scope screen and compare to the Figma screenshot; spot-check computed styles in the browser (not just class names). {"id":"pbh-bq8","title":"Resume booking modal at the first incomplete step after email submit","description":"After the user submits their email in the marketing booking flow, resume them at the correct point. NEW users go straight into the modal at the first step; RETURNING (known) users see a "Welcome back" screen and must confirm via an emailed link before resuming at their first incomplete step. If everything is already complete, hand off to the funnel.

Figma:
- Welcome-back screen ("Already in database"): https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=896-1479&m=dev

## Flow
1. Booking form email submit -> resolveBookingProgress(email) looks up the user.
2. NEW email -> create user (createAccountCore) -> open modal at "details" (no confirmation needed; nothing to protect).
3. RETURNING email (user exists, not fully complete) -> show the "Welcome back, {firstName}" modal (Figma 896-1479) and SEND a confirmation email. Do NOT open the step modal yet.
4. User clicks the emailed magic link -> verify token -> resume the booking modal at the FIRST INCOMPLETE step (details -> consent -> payment) computed by resolveBookingProgress.
5. Already fully complete (details + consent + succeeded payment) -> hand off to funnel /login?email= (same as DoneStep) -> /assessments.

## Welcome back screen (Figma 896-1479, "Extra Information" card)
- Title: "Welcome back, {firstName}"
- Body: "You already started the process previously. We’ve sent you an email. Please check your inbox, and confirm this is you."
- CTA: "Continue Where I left" (re-send/return affordance; the actual resume happens via the emailed link).
- Rendered as a modal/card over the booking section; reuse the existing Modal shell (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/Modal.tsx) + @pbh/ui + tokens.

## Current behavior (to change)
- BookingStepFlow.tsx uses a useState stepIndex over MODAL_STEPS = ["details","consent","payment","done"]; start() HARDCODES setStepIndex(0). advance() uses Math.min, so starting mid-sequence already works.
- Email is collected by inline SignupForm (first/last/email) -> signupAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts) -> createAccountCore (packages/booking/src/server/signup-core.ts), which INSERTs a users row and REJECTS duplicate emails ("account already exists"). Must change to lookup-or-create.

## Completeness signals (all NEW reads; consents/payments are write-only today)
- details incomplete if users.dateOfBirth is null (also stateOfResidence, phone, gender, educationLevel, patientIdentification; message optional). packages/db/src/schema/users.ts; set by details-core.ts.
- consent incomplete if no consents row for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/consents.ts.
- payment incomplete if no payments row with status="succeeded" for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/payments.ts (fulfill.ts recordSucceededPayment). A bare row is NOT sufficient (failed/refunded can exist).

## Implementation
1. resolveBookingProgress core in packages/booking/src/server/ (e.g. booking-progress.ts): normalize email; SELECT users WHERE email = ? (pattern in register-and-enroll.ts:499-519). No user -> createAccountCore -> step "details" (new-user path). User exists -> first incomplete step, or "complete". Returns { userId, email, firstName, step:"details"|"consent"|"payment"|"complete", isReturning:boolean }.
2. Returning + not complete -> render Welcome back modal + trigger sendResumeConfirmationEmail(userId). Wire signupAction accordingly.
3. Extend SignupState/SignupResult (packages/booking/src/types.ts) to carry step + isReturning (+ complete).
4. BookingStepFlow.start(): for the new-user path, setStepIndex(Math.max(0, MODAL_STEPS.indexOf(step))); for returning, show Welcome back modal instead; if step==="complete", navigate to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_FUNNEL_URL}/login?email=... (reuse DoneStep handoff).
5. Magic-link resume: verify route validates the token and opens the booking modal at the resolved first-incomplete step.

## Email confirmation infrastructure (NEW PREREQUISITE - none exists today)
There is NO email-sending setup in the repo (no resend/nodemailer/sendgrid/ses, no token/verify code). This feature needs:
- An email-sending capability + provider (recommend Resend; works cleanly on Vercel) + a confirmation email template.
- A confirmation token: signed (HMAC/JWT, short TTL) OR a DB table (e.g. booking_resume_tokens with expiry) tied to userId + intended step; single-use.
- A verify/resume route that validates the token and enters the resumed flow.
This is sizable and separable; consider splitting it into its own prerequisite sub-task that this one depends on.

## Security / privacy
The email confirmation is the mitigation for unauthenticated resume + PII/enumeration: DO NOT open the step modal or reveal stored data on bare email entry. To avoid account enumeration, show the same "we’ve sent you an email" outcome whether or not the email exists (only send the email when it does). Tokens must be single-use + short-lived. Revisit with real auth (resolveBookingUserId is a TODO(clerk)).

## Acceptance criteria
- New email -> modal opens at details (no email confirmation).
- Returning email (partial) -> Welcome back modal shown + confirmation email sent; step modal NOT opened until the emailed link is clicked; link resumes at the correct first incomplete step (consent if details done; payment if details+consent done).
- Fully-onboarded/paid email -> handed off to funnel /login -> /assessments.
- Bare email entry never reveals whether an account exists nor exposes stored PII; tokens single-use + expiring.
- Payment completeness uses status="succeeded", not just a row.

## Verification
Seed users at each state (new/partial/complete) in a test DB. pnpm --filter marketing dev (:3000); submit each email and confirm: new -> details; returning -> Welcome back + email; click link -> resumes at expected step; complete -> funnel handoff. pnpm typecheck + lint.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"brizolla.tuily@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-20T18:07:19Z","created_by":"tuily","updated_at":"2026-07-20T18:22:25Z"}

{"id":"pbh-chu","title":"Implement "Choose How to Start" first-login welcome screen (funnel)","description":"Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=1088-1628&m=dev

Post-login "Choose How to Start" screen in the funnel app. Headline + subcopy and two cards: "Talk to an Expert" (CTA: Start With Navigator) and "Start with Assessments" (CTA: Start Assessments). Shown ONLY on a user's first login.

## Decisions

- pnpm typecheck + lint changed files.

{"description":"Write the agreed HIPAA session-timeout control set into `docs/sow2/technical/auth-plan.md` so it survives the auth-provider decision. This is the record of the requirement; it does not depend on which provider wins.

Background (Stefanie, Slack): HIPAA does not prescribe a specific session-timeout duration — it requires an automatic logoff control based on the organization's risk assessment. Because the authenticated dashboard provides access to the Linus report, the dashboard session becomes part of the protected access pathway even though the report itself stays stored in Linus.

Controls to document:
- 15-minute inactivity timeout on the authenticated dashboard
- 8-hour absolute session cap, so an active session cannot remain authenticated indefinitely
- single-use sign-in link with a 10–15 minute TTL (applies if magic links are chosen)
- scope: the ENTIRE authenticated dashboard, not only the report page

Note: the doc's current "Session strategy" section specifies a 30-day sliding expiration. That must be replaced, not appended to.

Deliberately NOT included: a step-up re-authentication gate before opening or downloading the report. Stefanie raised it in the original thread, but it was dropped from scope — the idle + absolute timeouts are the control set we are committing to. Revisit only if compliance asks for it again.
"}

{"id":"pbh-140","title":"Rename the funnel app to "app" — it is not a funnel anymore","description":"`apps/funnel` is no longer a funnel. The signup → details → consent → payment funnel now lives in the marketing app (`apps/marketing/src/components/booking/`, built on `@pbh/booking`); what remains in `apps/funnel` is the authenticated post-purchase product — the assessments dashboard, report download, and login. The name now misleads anyone reading the tree.

Rename the directory and the workspace package to `app` (`apps/app`, package name `app`).

Known touch points (not exhaustive — grep `funnel` after moving):

Build / deploy config:
- `apps/funnel/package.json:2` — `"name": "funnel"`, plus the `dev`/`start` port flags
- `apps/funnel/vercel.json` — `"ignoreCommand": "npx turbo-ignore funnel"` must become the new package name, or preview builds will stop being skipped correctly
- root `tsconfig.json` — path references to `apps/funnel`
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` needs no change (globs `apps/*`), but `pnpm-lock.yaml` will need regenerating via `pnpm install`
- `.claude/settings.local.json` has funnel-scoped entries

Vercel:
- the Vercel project for this app has its **Root Directory** set to `apps/funnel` — that setting must be updated in the Vercel dashboard in the SAME change, or the deploy breaks. This is the step most likely to be forgotten.
- `pnpm --filter funnel …` appears in CI/docs/CLAUDE.md commands

Code + docs:
- `apps/funnel/src/app/robots.ts`, `next.config.ts`, `.env.example`, `src/app/page.tsx`
- `CLAUDE.md` "Workspace layout" section documents `apps/funnel/`
- ~17 files under `docs/` reference the funnel app, including `docs/sow2/technical/monorepo-plan.md`, `flow-diagrams.md`, and `diagrams/system-architecture.mmd`/`.svg`

Separately (decide whether to include or split out): the word "funnel" is used throughout `packages/booking/**` doc comments to mean "the non-marketing app" (e.g. `ConsentForm.tsx:45` "shared by the funnel and the marketing modal", `types.ts:4`, `webhook.ts:14`). Those comments become wrong once the funnel lives in marketing. Suggest fixing them in the same pass so the rename is not half-done.

Do this on a quiet branch — it touches nearly every workspace file and will conflict with anything in flight.

{"id":"pbh-eaj","title":"Rebuild booking section: two packages + signup in the modal","description":"Rebuild the marketing booking section to the two-product design, and move signup into the modal.

Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=1088-4452&m=dev

## The design (node 1088:4452)

Section header "Start with a brain health consultation" + subcopy, then **two side-by-side package cards** (610px each), then a full-width HSA/FSA note: "Both services may be eligible for HSA/FSA reimbursement, depending on your plan. We can provide documentation to support submission."

**Basic Assessment Package — $149** — CTA "Book Basic Assessment"
- Brain health assessment (taken online)
- A personal consultation with a brain health specialist
- Clear explanation of findings and risk profile
- Personalized lifestyle recommendations and next steps

**Comprehensive Assessment Package — $449** — CTA "Book Comprehensive Assessment"
- Everything in the Basic Assessment.
- Physician Assessment.
- A diagnosis from a clinician
- Ongoing treatment options with medication and doctor referrals
- Continuous support from a brain health specialist

**There is no inline signup form in this design.** Each card's CTA opens the booking modal, which now starts at signup.

## What this touches

- `apps/marketing/src/components/booking/BookingSection.tsx` — currently a two-column layout: copy + inline `SignupForm` on the left, a single `IncludesPanel` on the right. Becomes header + two cards + the HSA/FSA note.
- `apps/marketing/src/components/booking/IncludesPanel.tsx` — currently hardcodes one price and six bullets. Becomes a reusable card taking name/price/bullets/CTA. Its inline check SVG should use `CheckIcon` from `@pbh/ui` (added in PR #20) or `PhosphorIcon name="SealCheck"` — the design uses SealCheck.
- `apps/marketing/src/components/booking/BookingStepFlow.tsx` — `MODAL_STEPS` is currently `["details","consent","payment","done"]` with signup inline on the page. Add `signup` as the first modal step and open the modal from each card's CTA. This resolves the open question flagged on PR #22: every Figma frame draws signup as a modal card, but it was left inline because moving it was out of that PR's scope.

## Known blockers — these are the real work, not the layout

1. **Pricing is single-product.** `packages/payments/src/pricing.ts` resolves ONE price from `STRIPE_ASSESSMENT_PRICE_ID` (`env.ts:27`) and memoises it in a module-level `cached` singleton. Two packages need two Stripe prices, a per-package lookup, and a cache keyed by package rather than one slot. `checkout-core.ts` builds the Session from that single entry.
2. **The chosen package isn't captured anywhere.** `payments` records only `amount_cents` — no price/product reference. The selection has to be carried from the card CTA through signup → details → consent → payment, and stored, or we can't tell afterwards which package someone bought.
3. **Comprehensive is not just a bigger Linus enrollment.** "Physician Assessment", "A diagnosis from a clinician", and "Ongoing treatment options with medication and doctor referrals" are clinical services beyond the Linus assessment. Decide what the funnel actually provisions for $449 — a different Linus campaign (`packages/linus/src/campaigns.ts`), a manual clinical workflow, or something else. **Confirm with David/Stefanie before building.** This also has compliance weight: "a diagnosis from a clinician" moves the product further from the wellness framing the consent copy currently uses.

## Open questions
- Does the $449 package change the consent text? The current wellness + HIPAA NPP consent (`pbh-3v0`) is written for a wellness assessment, not a diagnostic service.
- Should the two cards be Tina-editable, or hardcoded? `BookingSection` currently takes `headline`/`subheadline` as props bound to a Tina block.

## Acceptance criteria
- Section matches the frame: header, two package cards with the exact copy above, HSA/FSA note.
- Each CTA opens the booking modal starting at signup; the chosen package is carried through the flow and recorded.
- Checkout charges the correct Stripe price per package (from the catalog, not a hardcoded amount — see pbh-ggr / PR #16).
- Matches Figma in-browser (computed styles, not class names); no raw hex.
- `pnpm typecheck` + lint changed files.
